teaser: Eight months of SG/Send, checked against its own briefs and commits: how file sharing became sgit and vaults, the pace, and what the market said.
core_idea: SG/Send began as file sharing where the server holds nothing, went live five days after its first commit, took payments within three weeks, and through folders, zips, a data room and the decision to copy Git became sgit and the vaults; the public record of 4,476 app commits, 1,620 command-line commits, 739 tags and 1,389 briefs corrects the founder's memory of the order, shows a fast February to May, a turn to focus in June, pauses and an October burst, shows the agents writing the code while the founder wrote briefs and merged, and records early that users bought credits and did not come back: the technology worked before the use case did.

figures.caption: Eight months of SG/Send and sgit, week by week: commits per week across all branches of the SG/Send app (bars) and the sgit command line (line), from 8 February to 14 October 2026, with the milestones the briefs and commits record and the command line's two long pauses shaded.

The order I remembered, and the order the record shows: the memo's sequence on the left, the same steps dated from the briefs and commits on the right. The vault and the data room were named in February, before folders, zips and Git.

sgit's unit tests as recorded in its commit messages, from 237 on 5 March to 4,232 on 14 October, and its releases to PyPI per month: the tests grew fastest from March to May; the releases came in bursts.
